key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized direct drive friction welding parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 joint strength, while deep learning can predict weld performance from process settings.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aerospace/automotive aluminum joints by pairing geometry-driven mechanical interlocking with data-driven process optimization.
method: Designed DDFW experiments with an L18 orthogonal array across friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time.
Tested a novel drilled-to-bossed geometry against conventional flat-to-flat joints to improve interlocking and weld integrity.
Trained deep learning models, including an ensemble residual network, compact attention network, and adaptive multiscale network, to predict ultimate tensile strength.
evidence_signal: The best setting achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the top predictor reached an R² of about 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model performance is moderate rather than near-perfect, so broader validation on more data and conditions would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
